LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How do we express the quantity or amount of something?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in texts
2. use determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in sentences correctly

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes

Teach
• Focus skill: identify determiners some, enough, each, and a lot of, in texts.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we express the quantity or amount of something?
2. Why should we give the exact amount of something?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
